text:
Florida's season has a family subplot running through it. Brady Tkachuk now plays beside his brother Matthew, and the two have generated more headlines than anyone on the roster, from Brady's taunt of his old Senators teammates to Matthew questioning whether Ottawa really sold out the building for the homecoming. On the ice, the reunion works. Sam Bennett with the Tkachuks is Florida's most-used line and wins 62% of the expected goals, and Brady scored twice in Saturday's loss in Washington with Matthew assisting both.

The Panthers are 9-6-2 with 53% of the expected goals, and their results sit almost exactly on their chances. That's a good team, not yet a dominant one, which is why our simulations land at 94 points and a 55% playoff chance. Seth Jones has been the surprise, with Sports Illustrated floating him as a Norris candidate after his October, and his pairing with Niko Mikkola has outscored opponents 11-6.

The worry is depth. Anton Lundell is day-to-day, and Sandis Vilmanis left Saturday's game after a Tom Wilson hit. Vilmanis has quietly been one of the best on-ice players on the team, with 63% of the five-on-five expected goals, and he plays on both of the other lines that are winning their minutes. Florida also takes 5.2 penalties a game, the kind of habit that turns close games into coin flips. Watch the bottom six this week: that's where this team gets tested.
